precepts.text: Blessed is he that readeth and they that hear the words of this prophecy and keep those things written therein: the laws of the Most High.
precepts.point: I will yet make doctrine to shine as the morning and pour out doctrine as prophecy, and leave it to all ages for ever. I have not laboured for myself only, but for all them that seek wisdom. We do not do this work for ourselves.

note.label: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

precepts.why:
Sirach says “I will yet pour out doctrine as prophecy, and leave it to all ages for ever.” With a war between America and Iran unfolding and many prophecies being fulfilled, we look at what the Bible says about prophecy itself.

“Blessed is he that readeth, and they that hear the words of this prophecy, and keep those things which are written therein: for the time is at hand.” Blessed is he that reads and hears, and keeps the things written therein. What is written in the scriptures? The laws of the Most High God.

So the blessing is not only in reading the prophecy but in keeping the law. We are blessed when we read and keep the things written in the law, because the time is at hand, and the doctrine poured out as prophecy was left for all ages, including ours.

precepts.text: A more sure word of prophecy, whereunto ye do well to take heed, as a light shining in a dark place. We are that light; through our example we win our people, whether in DC, New Orleans, California, or the UK. No prophecy is of private interpretation; holy black and Hispanic men of God spake as moved by the Holy Ghost.
precepts.point: I will yet make doctrine to shine as the morning and pour out doctrine as prophecy, and leave it to all ages for ever. I have not laboured for myself only, but for all them that seek wisdom. We do not do this work for ourselves.

note.label: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

precepts.why:
“I will yet make doctrine to shine as the morning, and will send forth her light afar off.” Peter says, “We have also a more sure word of prophecy; whereunto ye do well that ye take heed”. Take heed to do what the scriptures say. The Most High called us into this truth, so we have to take heed.

“as unto a light that shineth in a dark place, until the day dawn, and the day star arise in your hearts”. We are that light shining in a dark place. That is why Christ said, let your light so shine before men. We have to be that example for our people, to win them over into the faith. Whether you are in DC, New Orleans, California or the UK, the Most High chose us, and through our example we have to win our people over.

“Knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture is of any private interpretation. For the prophecy came not in old time by the will of man: but holy men of God spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost.” Prophecy is the foretelling of future events in the Bible, and it did not come by the will of man. Holy men of God, holy black men, holy Hispanic men, spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost. That is the light sent forth afar off.

precepts.text: Speak in the ears of my people the words of prophecy, our people, not a people of strange speech; they are faithful and true. Fear not the imaginations against thee when you teach against America and governments, for all the unfaithful shall die in their unfaithfulness, and I will bring plagues upon the world, the sword, famine, death, and destruction.
precepts.point: I will yet make doctrine to shine as the morning and pour out doctrine as prophecy, and leave it to all ages for ever. I have not laboured for myself only, but for all them that seek wisdom. We do not do this work for ourselves.

note.label: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

precepts.why:
“Behold, speak thou in the ears of my people the words of prophecy, which I will put in thy mouth, saith the Lord”. Speak in the ears of my people. That is why in Ezekiel he said not to go to a people of a strange speech: we have to deal with our people.

“And cause them to be written in paper: for they are faithful and true.” Everything written in the Bible is faithful and true.

“Fear not the imaginations against thee, let not the incredulity of them trouble thee, that speak against thee. For all the unfaithful shall die in their unfaithfulness.” Do not fear what the nations are going to do to us for teaching against America and against governments. The Bible says do not fear.

“Behold, saith the Lord, I will bring plagues upon the world; the sword, famine, death, and destruction.” The Most High says he is going to bring judgment upon the world. That is the doctrine Sirach says was poured out as prophecy and left to all ages, and we do not labour for ourselves only: we speak it in the ears of our people.

precepts.text: Be ye strong and let not your hands be weak, for your work shall be rewarded. When Asa heard the prophecy of Oded he took courage and put away the abominable idols out of all the land. That is what prophecy is for: courage to let go of idols and secret sins. As the war unfolds, more Israelites repent and wake up.
precepts.point: I will yet make doctrine to shine as the morning and pour out doctrine as prophecy, and leave it to all ages for ever. I have not laboured for myself only, but for all them that seek wisdom. We do not do this work for ourselves.

note.label: America At War With Iran: Preparation For Conflict

precepts.why:
When we teach the Bible and bring out the prophecy, in the street or in classes, what are these scriptures supposed to do for our people? The prophet told King Asa: “Be ye strong therefore, and let not your hands be weak: for your work shall be rewarded.” The days we are living in now are not the time for us to be weak.

“And when Asa heard these words, and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage, and put away the abominable idols out of all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and out of the cities which he had taken from mount Ephraim”. When Asa heard the words of the prophecy, he took courage.

That is what prophecy is supposed to do for us: give us the courage to let go of our idols and our secret sins. We are seeing prophecy unravel right before our eyes: Iran and Israel going to war, and now America getting involved. It was a rumor and talk for years, and now we see it unfold. That means more Israelites are repenting, and more of our brothers and our people are waking up. That is the doctrine poured out as prophecy, laboured for all them that seek wisdom.

precepts.text: He filleth all things with his wisdom, as Phison and as Tigris in the time of the new fruits.
precepts.point: Sirach names the same rivers as the flow of understanding, and the sea of glass is that clear water in heaven.

note.label: The Kingdom Of Adam And The Old World

precepts.why:
“And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became into four heads.” The first is Pison, which compasses the land of Havilah, where there is gold; the second is Gihon, compassing the whole land of Ethiopia; the third is Hiddekel, going toward the east of Assyria; and the fourth is Euphrates. The Most High is doing two things here. It is a similitude of the waters above, since he divided the waters below from the waters above. And it goes into rulership: there are trees by those rivers, and that is Adam's governance. It speaks of the heavens, but it came down on the earth too.

Sirach 24 names the same rivers: “He filleth all things with his wisdom, as Phison and as Tigris in the time of the new fruits. He maketh the understanding to abound like Euphrates, and as Jordan in the time of the harvest. He maketh the doctrine of knowledge appear as the light, and as Geon in the time of vintage.” These are the four rivers of Genesis, and the water is wisdom and understanding. What went forth through all those rivers was the wisdom of God, going to Adam's sons ruling this earth in righteousness. It starts in the heavens, and it is on the earth too.

“The first man knew her not perfectly: no more shall the last find her out.” The first man is Adam, and he did not know wisdom perfectly because he sinned. Wisdom is infinite. “For her thoughts are more than the sea, and her counsels profounder than the great deep.” The great deep is space.

“I also came out as a brook from a river, and as a conduit into a garden. I said, I will water my best garden, and will water abundantly my garden bed: and, lo, my brook became a river, and my river became a sea.” The best garden is paradise. The brook became a river and the river became a sea, and that sea is the sea of glass in heaven.

precepts.text: Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee: David recites what the Father said to the Son, and the moment he was made the nations were given him for his inheritance.
precepts.point: He that made me caused my tabernacle to rest, and said, Let thy dwelling be in Jacob: he was made, and the rest he was given was a body.

precepts.text: A lot of people, meaning the other nations, think this Bible pertains to them, but it does not; you might find them in the Bible, but they are not of the Bible.
precepts.point: He established a testimony in Jacob and appointed a law in Israel, which He commanded our fathers to make known to their children, so the generation to come and the children yet to be born might know them, declare them to their children, set their hope in God, and keep His commandments.

note.label: Psalm 78: The History of Israel's Rebellion and the Choosing of Judah and David

precepts.why:
“For he established a testimony in Jacob, and appointed a law in Israel, which he commanded our fathers, that they should make them known to their children”. The law was appointed in Israel, for Israel to hand down to their children, that they might set their hope in God and keep his commandments.

Ecclesiasticus says the same about the whole book: “All these things are the book of the covenant of the most high God, even the law which Moses commanded for an heritage unto the congregations of Jacob.” The law is an heritage unto the congregations of Jacob.

A lot of people, meaning the other nations, think this Bible pertains to them, but it does not. You might find them in the Bible, but they are not of the Bible. The testimony was established in Jacob and the law appointed in Israel, and it was commanded to our fathers to pass to our children.
